title: Briefing for 2026-11-11
intro: Good morning. Here is your briefing for 2026-11-11: US markets, global news, and the Philippines, in five minutes.
us: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than expected, complicating Fed's inflation fight. China's goods surplus tops $1 trillion for a second year amid calls for Beijing to rebalance trade. 3 unexpected reasons the October jobs report was so strong. A key report for where inflation stood in October comes out Tuesday. Here's what to expect. China wholesale inflation hits highest in more than four years as consumer measure slows. U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, way more than expected; unemployment rate slips to 4.1%.
global: Meghan's father Thomas Markle back in federal custody after allegedly removing ankle monitor. 'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El Niño with floods predicted. Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government. Poundland hopeful for last-minute rescue deal to stave off collapse. Claude chatbot maker set for $1.3tn stock market debut despite 'catastrophic' AI warning. Sales of tinned food and bottled water jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch.
philippines: LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. Abando returns to Gilas as debuting Boatwright banners new FIBA roster. Oil dependence is bad for the climate and the economy, UN chief tells COP31. SPECIAL COVERAGE: Impeachment trial of Sara Duterte.
outro: That's your briefing. Have a great day.
